title: ac-bdd template variables
description: Values for templates/ac-bdd.md.j2 and templates/ac-bdd.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from ac-bdd.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

author.title: Author
author.description: Who wrote these criteria. Ambiguity gets resolved by asking a person, and "the team" is not a person you can ask on the day the build is red.

error_scenario_name.title: Error scenario name
error_scenario_name.description: Name of the failure scenario. Every set needs at least one - a story with no failure path does not lack failures, it lacks tested ones.

happy_path_name.title: Happy path name
happy_path_name.description: Four or five words naming the main scenario - the path when nothing goes wrong. It becomes the test name people quote in standup, so make it readable out loud.

perf_threshold.title: Perf threshold
perf_threshold.description: The performance criterion as a number and a percentile - "p95 under 2s with 50 concurrent users". "Fast" is not testable and will be argued about the week after release.

requirement_summary.title: Requirement summary
requirement_summary.description: What the story delivers, one sentence, from the user's side. If you cannot say it without naming a table or an endpoint, you are describing a task and the criteria will test the wrong thing.

security_rule.title: Security rule
security_rule.description: The role-based rule this story must enforce, by role and action - "only Admin may delete records". Say who may NOT do it as well; that half is what gets missed.

story_id.title: Story id
story_id.description: The tracker id these criteria belong to (PROJ-412). Criteria that float free of a story get re-litigated in QA, by people who were not in the refinement session.
